checks.finding: All six requirements (REQ-001..REQ-006) resolve to concrete, measurable acceptance criteria: file-content assertions with named elements (AC-001, AC-007, AC-009), exit-code and file-existence assertions (AC-003, AC-005), and elapsed-wall-clock plus process-liveness assertions with stated thresholds (AC-004). No in-scope requirement rests on unmeasurable intent.

Overview's two stated goals (close the hung-panelist timeout hole for #133; close the THREAT-MODEL checklist/surface gaps for #134) and its 'consumer-visible consequence' claim (hung panelist fails the gate instead of hanging it) each trace to specific ACs: AC-003..AC-006 for the timeout goal, AC-007/AC-008/AC-013/AC-009/AC-010/AC-014 for the documentation goal, and AC-006 specifically for the gate-fails consequence.

Acceptance criteria are stated as externally observable file content, exit codes, elapsed time, and process liveness (e.g. AC-004: 'measuring elapsed wall-clock time against the bound, and by confirming the stub process is no longer alive'; AC-008: anti-padding row-count assertions). No AC relies on subjective or intent-based language.

Non-goals section is explicit and covers the boundaries most likely to expand: retries, restating the already-correct absent/error path, adding new output-validation code, re-documenting the Codex agent-role surface, changing check-cross-model's own logic, and pinning/vendoring CLIs.

Baseline Constraints (BL-001..BL-005) and Assumptions state behaviour-preservation, gate-non-modification, additive-not-replacement text changes, dual-runtime parity, and the protected-file/human-copy boundary (BL-005, directly verified against guard-invariants.generated.js:5, INV-017). Migration and approval boundaries are addressed.

The core round-3 asymmetry argument (no PowerShell (b) sub-case; TerminateProcess cannot be trapped the way SIGTERM can) is sound and its replacement (the no-orphan assertion tied to Kill($true)'s tree-kill semantics) is a genuine, failable property, not a rationalization. However, this same replacement introduces an unexamined coverage asymmetry: the AC-004 runtime table and the TEST-004 runtime table give PowerShell's (a) sub-case a no-orphan-of-grandchild assertion ('the stub spawns its own child, and neither survives the runner's return'), justified by Kill($true)'s tree-kill semantics, but define no equivalent assertion for POSIX. The POSIX 'Bound mechanism'/'Escalation' columns describe kill -0 polling and SIGTERM/SIGKILL against a single tracked PID, with no stated process-group semantics (no setsid/negative-PID signaling committed anywhere in the document), so nothing in this specification guarantees or tests that a grandchild spawned by the POSIX vendor-CLI stub is killed rather than orphaned -- the exact risk Edge Case 2 names ('leaves an orphan holding the API session') and which is runtime-agnostic. Unlike the (b) asymmetry, which is explained by a citable OS-level distinction, this asymmetry has no stated justification in the text: the no-orphan assertion is framed purely as compensation for PowerShell losing sub-case (b), not as evidence POSIX is structurally exempt from the same risk. A task author cannot tell whether the POSIX kill mechanism is required to reach descendant processes, and no test would catch it either way -- the same class of gap this document already corrected three times for AC-003/AC-004/AC-005, now reproduced in the opposite direction.

No domain/ directory exists at the repository root (verified via Glob for domain/context-map.md and domain/domain-contract.json), so this check's applicability precondition is not met. Recorded as skipped per the calibration rule.
